findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - The following foods were observed to be at temperatures of 47F-52F in the prep cooler; 1. American cheese slices in top holding area; 2. gallon of mayo (1/2 full); 3. gallon of ranch (1/2 full); 4. gallon of blue cheese (1/2 full); 5. squeeze bottles of Italian dressing, mayo, blue cheese, mayo, & tartar sauce. All questionable products were discarded.
Cook was gone for the day by the time temperatures were checked. Some of the bottles may have been out during lunch. However, the bottom shelf inside the prep cooler is jam packed full of product. Cooler is holding at 41F/below but having lots of products stored in the cooler can inhibit proper air flow. Be careful to not overfill coolers in order for air to adequately circulate and help maintain foods at 41F/below in coolers. Also, if dressings are left out at lunch/dinner time then use/discard within 4 hrs. 
Maintain cold potentially hazardous food at 41F/below or establish and adhere to a time control policy (use/discard w/in 4hrs) if squeeze bottles/containers will be left out during lunch/dinner.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Cook was observed placing frozen ground beef in the reach-in cooler as inspector was walking into the kitchen. When asked how long the beef had been out at room temperature he noted for ~5 minutes, and then noted long enough for him to eat half a sandwich. He said it was going to take awhile to thaw and wouldn't even be thawed by tomorrow. Cook was advised frozen potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must not be set out at room temperature to thaw for any length of time. Cook stated he understood.
PHF shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - House flies (~9-10 total) were observed in the men's room, in kitchen by mopsink, at the bar, and around the front door/windows.
